look_here_first: Look below the whole flower cluster: Tinantia anomala has an exposed, one-sided cyme above an open, mostly flat leaflike bract. The green sepals around individual buds are not a fused spathe pocket. Then check Joey's macro for purple-and-yellow filament beards: six fertile stamens, five filaments bearded. Commelina erecta instead has a folded spathe pocket and smooth filaments.

lookalikes.differences: Commelina erecta: Commelina erecta has the unmistakable folded/fused green spathe pocket enclosing buds and fruit. Tinantia instead has an open leaflike bract subtending an exposed terminal cyme; its upper leaves also more strongly clasp the stem. Tradescantia spp.: Tradescantia spiderworts usually have three comparably showy petals. Tinantia has two large blue/lavender petals plus one much smaller white petal, and its one-sided cyme/bract architecture differs. Commelina benghalensis: Tropical spiderwort/dayflower is an invasive Commelina with a true spathe and often reddish hairs on leaf sheaths. Tinantia lacks that Commelina spathe pocket and carries its flowers on an open terminal cyme.
